headline: IAMGOLD LIFTS Côté to 20.3M oz — 12% Resource Jump Triggers Q4 Mine Expansion Study
snippet: IAMGOLD released a consolidated mineral resource estimate for its Côté Gold mine on June 1, integrating the adjacent Gosselin zone into a single block model and lifting total M&I resources 12% to 20.34 million oz at 0.75 g/t Au. A mine expansion study targeting a larger pit and plant is expected in Q4 2026.

headline: GOLD JUMPS $54 to $4,514 as Iran-US Strikes Revive Inflation Trade — Experts Eye $4,800 June Ceiling
snippet: Gold touched $4,514/oz on June 2 — up $54 from the prior session — after renewed Iran-US strikes pushed oil higher and revived inflation fears; silver sits near $75, well below its May peak of $89.4. Experts polled by CBS forecast gold in a $4,400–$4,800 range through June, with JP Morgan seeing silver average $81/oz for the full year.

headline: PAN AMERICAN SILVER commits C$201M to Bell Creek Shaft Extension — Vogel and Samson Deposits Now in Sight
snippet: Pan American Silver approved a $146M (C$201M) first-phase expansion at its Bell Creek gold mine in Timmins, Ontario, on June 1, committing to a 625-metre shaft deepening plus exploration drifts toward the Vogel and Samson deposits. On-site work begins July 2026; commissioning is targeted for H1 2029.

headline: DATA CENTER POWER RACE: Load Up on Nuclear and Uranium ETFs Before the AI Surge Hits the Grid
snippet: The DOE projects AI data centers will consume up to 12% of US electricity by 2028, and analysts say uranium and nuclear stocks are still early in their re-rating. Spot uranium is trading near $85/lb while utilities rebuild contract books and tech giants sign SMR supply deals; three ETFs covering reactors, uranium miners and smart grid are highlighted.

headline: SIX STRAIGHT YEARS: Silver Supply Deficit Widens as Junior Explorers Race to Fill the Gap
snippet: Silver has now posted six consecutive years of supply deficit, with the 2026 shortfall widening 15% to approximately 46 million oz as industrial demand from AI infrastructure, EVs and power grids offsets a slowdown in solar PV consumption. Cumulative drawdowns of above-ground COMEX and LBMA inventories since 2021 have now exceeded 762 million oz.

headline: CHILE COPPER COLLAPSE: Output Down 13.8% in April — Seven-Month Slide Deepens 330,000-Tonne Global Deficit
snippet: Chile's copper production fell 13.8% year-on-year in April 2026, extending a seven-month streak of declines driven by ore grade deterioration at Codelco and other major producers; Q1 output was down 5.8% on the same basis. JP Morgan now projects a 2026 refined copper deficit of 330,000 tonnes, with copper trading near $6.56/lb on tight supply expectations.

headline: LITHIUM DEMAND TURNS: Energy Storage Set for 31% of Global Consumption by End of 2026
snippet: A boom in grid-scale battery storage has materially lifted the demand outlook for lithium after two years of oversupply pressure; broker Guotai Junan projects energy storage will account for 31% of total lithium carbonate equivalent consumption in 2026, up from 23% in 2025. Analysts say the shift could accelerate the supply-demand rebalance to H2 2026.

headline: MINERS FINALLY RE-RATE: Gold Producers Printing Record Free Cash Flow at $4,500 Gold But Still Trading at a Discount
snippet: With gold above $4,500/oz and all-in sustaining costs mostly below $2,000/oz, senior producers are generating margins that translate into 30–50% free cash flow expansion per 10–15% gold price move — yet miners continue to trade at a discount to net asset value. Newmont and Barrick combined for $8.8 billion in FCF in 2025 while returning 40–50% to shareholders.

headline: CHINA RAISES Rare Earth Prices 44% in Q2 — Seventh Straight Quarterly Increase Pressures Western Buyers
snippet: China Northern Rare Earth Group set Q2 2026 concentrate prices at 38,804 yuan/tonne — a 44% jump quarter-on-quarter and the seventh consecutive quarterly increase — driven by tightening domestic quotas, sulfuric acid export restrictions and surging EV and wind turbine demand. Western producers including Lynas, MP Materials and USA Rare Earth are racing to fill the gap.

headline: TSX-V SURGE: Junior Mining Stocks Rally as Global Supply Scarcity Narrative Drives Capital Rotation
snippet: Junior mining stocks on the TSX Venture Exchange are outperforming as improving commodity sentiment — led by gold above $4,500 and copper near multi-year highs — revives retail and institutional appetite for speculative exploration names. Analysts point to supply scarcity across gold, copper and critical minerals as the structural driver behind the rotation.

headline: QUEBEC M&A: Edison Lithium Advances Joutel Gold Acquisition — Historical Core Confirms Exploration Upside
snippet: Edison Lithium has located historical drill core during a property visit to the Joutel North-West and Gagné gold-copper properties in Quebec being acquired from Globex Mining, adding confidence to the resource potential ahead of closing. The Abitibi-Greenstone Belt deal highlights continued M&A activity as explorers pivot to gold-exposed Quebec targets.
